item.title: Nvidia Q3 Revenue Doubles to $115.8B as CEO Huang Resigns Amid Scandal
item.description:
Nvidia Q3 Revenue Doubles to $115.8B as CEO Huang Resigns Amid Scandal

Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, more than double the prior year, while its stock plunged nearly 40 percent from an October high following the resignation of cofounder and CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of extramarital affairs and a Chinese espionage plot.

📊 Q3 Financial Results

  • Revenue more than doubled year over year to $115.8 billion
  • Data center revenue increased 110 percent
  • Results exceeded Wall Street expectations
  • Nearly $20 billion in revenue came from the Vera Rubin platform

🖥️ Vera Rubin Platform

  • Shipped during the quarter
  • Described as the “fastest product ramp in company history” by Kress
  • Generated nearly $20 billion in revenue

📉 Stock Price Volatility

  • All-time high reached on October 6
  • October 29: closed at $213.66, down 0.8 percent
  • October 30: closed with a 4 percent drop as Nasdaq fell 2.9 percent
  • November 4: continued decline amid midterm election concerns
  • November 5: fell 9.2 percent, largest single-day drop in at least a year
  • November 6: rose 2.8 percent to $186.64
  • November 9: tumbled 7 percent at open, volume surged past three-month average
  • November 10: closed at $168.89, nearly 10 percent below last trading day of 2025
  • November 11: rebounded slightly then plunged again on ouster reports
  • November 12: fell nearly 14 percent at open, closed with 4.3 percent dip, intraday low $148.80 (lowest in a year)
  • By Thursday (November 12) hovering around $150, wiping out post-earnings pop from Tuesday night

🧑‍💼 Leadership Crisis

  • October 29: The New York Times reported U.S. intelligence believed Huang was target of Chinese espionage plot
  • Plot centered on “close relationship” with Alice Huang, Chinese national and executive at Megaspeed (Singapore data center company, Nvidia client)
  • November 8: Huang sent company-wide memo apologizing for extramarital affair
  • Memo coincided with independent board investigation into alleged misconduct and potential compromise of company secrets or national security
  • November 11: media reports indicated board considering ousting Huang; second alleged affair with Nvidia employee emerged
  • November 12: Nvidia announced Huang’s departure
  • Harvey Jones appointed chairman of the board; stated company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and retained executive search firm for replacement
  • Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and led it without a succession plan

🏛️ Congressional Hearings

  • December 1: Huang scheduled for transcribed interviews before House Foreign Affairs Committee, Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and House Intelligence Committee
  • December 2: Nvidia general counsel scheduled for same committees

🤖 Anthropic Debut

  • Anthropic, a major Nvidia customer, made Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share — 34 percent higher than expected

#Nvidia #JensenHuang #VeraRubin #AIChips #StockMarket #CongressionalHearings

item.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Architecture Debuts in MLPerf Training v6.1
item.description:
NVIDIA Vera Rubin Architecture Debuts in MLPerf Training v6.1

NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin architecture has made its debut in MLPerf Training v6.1, showcasing impressive performance and scalability. The new architecture, along with its CUDA software stack, has demonstrated significant advancements in AI training capabilities.

🔍 Overview

  • MLPerf Training v6.1 marks the debut of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin architecture.
  • Vera Rubin NVL72 platform delivered the fastest time to train on six of the seven benchmarks.
  • NVIDIA platforms hold the fastest time to train on every benchmark in v6.1.
  • Vera Rubin successfully completed the entire suite in its inaugural run.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Vera Rubin NVL72 achieved up to 2x more performance than a highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 baseline.
  • For the DeepSeek-V3 671B benchmark, NVIDIA demonstrated massive scale on a 10,240-GPU GB300 NVL72 cluster.
  • Vera Rubin maintained above 97% overall efficiency when scaling from 256 to 1,024 GPUs.
  • NVIDIA platforms were the only ones to submit results across all seven benchmarks.

🚀 Availability

  • The Vera Rubin architecture is now available and has been tested in MLPerf Training v6.1.

💡 Why it Matters

  • The performance gains span the entire modeling pipeline, supporting everything from large-scale pretraining to reinforcement learning post-training.
  • The new architecture is designed to handle the most demanding workloads, including the 671-billion-parameter token-dropless Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model.
  • The Vera Rubin platform also proved its flexibility by submitting on two different inference backends: NVIDIA NeMo RL with TensorRT-LLM and with vLLM.
  • The NVIDIA Vera CPU is integral to the architecture, sustaining more than 22,500 concurrent RL environments across 256 CPUs in a single Vera CPU rack.

#NVIDIA #VeraRubin #MLPerf #AITraining #CUDA #DeepLearning

Source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Achieves up to 2x Blackwell Ultra Performance in MLPerf Training v6.1 | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Features Vera Rubin Support and Enhanced Multi-Process Service
item.description:
NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Features Vera Rubin Support and Enhanced Multi-Process Service

NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 has reached general availability, bringing the NVIDIA Vera Rubin architecture to enterprise production. This update provides new platform support, including Windows on Arm for DGX Station, and introduces advanced customization for GPU work scheduling through locality domains and Multi-Process Service (MPS) v3.

🔍 Overview

  • NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 achieves general availability (GA) across major new platforms.
  • NVIDIA Vera Rubin support has moved to GA, making it ready for enterprise production.
  • Windows on Arm support, which has been GA since CUDA 13.4, now extends to the NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows.
  • Enhanced GPU scheduling is introduced via locality domains and updated MPS controls.

⚙️ Key details

  • SM Resource Control: Applications can choose between uniform streaming multiprocessor (SM) partitions or utilize the cudaDevSmResourceGroupLocalityDomainSupplementalSms flag to include all available SMs in selected domains.
  • Driver Compatibility: Starting with the Rubin architecture, CUDA supports Windows Driver Display Model (WDDM) and Microsoft Compute Driver Model (MCDM), while Tesla Compute Cluster (TCC) is no longer supported.
  • CUDA Graph Enhancements: Support is added for batched 1D memory copies, enabling cudaMemcpyBatchAsync calls to be captured and replayed within reusable graph workflows.
  • CUDA Tile Kernels: Kernels can now perform direct multi-GPU communication and call SIMT library device functions from cuTile Python or CUDA Tile C++ on data already in registers or shared memory.

🧩 How it works

Feature Functionality
Weighted timeslicing Scales the base compute timeslice per MPS server to give longer compute turns to specific workloads.
SM partition load balancing Enables workloads to borrow capacity via --max-chunks and lend SMs when idle using --shareable=true.
Cgroup-based routing Maps cgroup v2 subtrees to MPS namespaces to route clients automatically through the daemon’s main socket.
Polling memory accounting Provides a fallback for usage and limit verification; forced via nvidia-cuda-mps-control memacct set force_polling=true.
Multi-GPU access Uses unicast pointers for NVLink-connected GPUs and multicast pointers for NVSwitch fabrics with NVLink SHARP support.

In addition to these features, applications can use discovery mode within the cudaDevSmResourceSplit() API to obtain partition SM counts. MPS v3 also ensures that borrowed resources are reclaimed before reassignment, while applications continue to see a stable base partition size.

🚀 Availability

  • Enterprise Production: NVIDIA Vera Rubin support is now in general availability.
  • Platform Extensions: Windows on Arm support is now available for NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows.

#CUDA #NVIDIA #VeraRubin #MPS #GPU

Source: NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Brings NVIDIA Vera Rubin GA Support | NVIDIA Technical Blog
